newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan plans further stock liberalisation.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan plans further stock liberalisation.

text.p: Taiwan plans to allow foreign firms to list their existing shares on its stock market in 1997 to meet the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum's trade liberalisation, a Finance Ministry official said on Tuesday.
The official said the liberalisation would allow foreign firms to raise funds on Taiwan's stock market through part of their existing shares instead of issuing Taiwan Depositary Receipts.
Currently, foreign firms can only list on Taiwan's stock market in the form of Taiwan Depositary Receipts and no foreign firms have applied for such listing so far.

The ministry would also allow Taiwanese companies to directly list their existing shares on foreign stock markets, relaxing current restrictions that only allow firms to list through Global Depositary Receipts, the official said.

"The liberalisation will make it easier for both foreign and local firms to raise funds in stock markets," another official at the ministry's Securities and Exchange Commission said. -- Taipei Newsroom (2-5080815)
